title: High-Pass Filter - Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD) for 5G NR Sub-6 GHz Front-End Module
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Pierre Dubois

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a High-Pass Filter filter targeting Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD) for 5G NR Sub-6 GHz Front-End Module. The filter is designed on AlN on Si substrate with a target center frequency of 4959.9 MHz and bandwidth of 185.6 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the 5G NR Sub-6 GHz Front-End Module module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: High-Pass Filter
- Frequency Band: Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD)
- Application: 5G NR Sub-6 GHz Front-End Module
- Substrate: AlN on Si
- Package: CSP (Chip Scale Package)
- Design Tool: PathWave EM Design
- Design Center: Singapore RF Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the High-Pass Filter design targeting Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       4959.9 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       185.6 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.1 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 20.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 40.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 23.0 dB
Q Factor:               10048
Temperature Coefficient:-21.3 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.4 x 1.2 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   5
Electrode Material:     Pt/Al
Passivation:            SiO2/Si3N4 stack
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open PathWave EM Design and load the High-Pass Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: AlN on Si with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 4959.9 MHz, BW 185.6 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.1 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (CSP (Chip Scale Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, AlN on Si).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Anritsu MS46122B ShockLine.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 14880 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.1 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 20.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 278 MHz offset >= 40.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 4 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 13.2 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +34 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 1000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 85%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2025-05-17
Devices Tested:         94
Insertion Loss (meas):  1.83 dB
Return Loss (meas):     21.5 dB
Rejection (meas):       43.5 dB
Isolation (meas):       28.1 dB
Q Factor (meas):        10048
Group Delay Variation:  1.6 ns
Power Handling:         +27 dBm
Die Yield:              93.6%

Result Classification:  NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The High-Pass Filter design demonstrated below-target performance for Band 40 (2300 MHz TDD).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Slight frequency drift observed at +85°C; TC layer thickness may need adjustment.
e) Cross-talk between adjacent filter channels was below -55 dB.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
